title: Layer Seven HTTP Reverse Proxy & Load Balancer in Go with Active Health Checks, Least-Connections & Circuit Breaking
problemStatement: Relying on opaque cloud provider load balancers obscures proxy-level concurrency bottlenecks, connection pool starvation, and subtle routing misconfigurations. Naive round-robin reverse proxies route traffic into dead sockets during upstream server crashes, lack connection draining during deployments, and fail to balance heterogeneous backend workloads. This project builds a high-performance Layer Seven application load balancer and reverse proxy from scratch in Go. The system implements multiple load balancing algorithms (round-robin, weighted round-robin, least-connections, and IP-hash), conducts active health checks with circuit breaking, performs graceful upstream draining during rotation, and exports Prometheus metrics.
useCases: Internal Microservice RPC Traffic Balancing: Platform engineering teams running private microservice meshes need lightweight, customizable L7 reverse proxies to distribute incoming traffic across backend service instances. The load balancer balances requests using least-connections to ensure long-running computational queries do not overwhelm individual backend pods. | Zero-Downtime Rolling Upstream Deployment Draining: Site reliability engineers require automated connection draining when deploying new application versions to prevent terminating active in-flight HTTP requests. The proxy marks graduating upstreams as draining, completing pending transactions while routing all new client requests to active backend nodes. | Session-Affinity E-Commerce Checkout Routing: E-commerce platforms maintaining in-memory shopping session state need deterministic client routing based on client IP addresses. The proxy implements consistent IP-hashing, mapping identical client IP addresses to dedicated backend instances while gracefully remapping upon backend changes.

title: Confidential Database Query Engine with Homomorphic Encryption

title: Secure Remote Code Execution Sandbox in Go with Linux Namespaces, cgroups v2 & seccomp BPF Syscall Filtering
problemStatement: Online code assessment platforms, interactive coding sandboxes, and continuous integration runners need to execute untrusted user-submitted code at high concurrency. This project builds a production-grade secure remote code execution engine and judge sandbox from scratch in Go. The system enforces strict process containment using Linux Namespaces (Mount, PID, Network, IPC, UTS), restricts CPU time and memory quotas with cgroups v2, filters dangerous kernel syscalls using seccomp BPF profiles, and executes code in under 120ms with zero host escape vulnerabilities.

The sandbox provides an ephemeral filesystem overlay, executing agent code with network isolation and returning execution outputs or stack traces safely. | Continuous Integration Micro-Build Container Runner: Developer platform teams need fast, lightweight sandboxes to run untrusted third-party pull request scripts and unit test suites. title: Full-Text Search Engine from Scratch in Go with Inverted Index, BM25 Scoring & Concurrent Segment Merging
problemStatement: Engineering teams building search interfaces often treat full-text search as an opaque black box provided by managed Elasticsearch or Solr clusters, leaving them unable to diagnose high heap memory churn, segment merge storm freezes, or unexpected relevance ranking degradation. Commercial search engines incur high infrastructure costs and severe memory overhead for small-to-medium embedded datasets. This project builds a production-grade full-text search engine from scratch in Go inspired by the Lucene architecture. The engine implements a custom text tokenizer with stop-word removal and Porter stemming, constructs memory-efficient inverted indexes with compressed posting lists using Roaring Bitmaps, executes the BM25 probabilistic relevance ranking algorithm, coordinates concurrent multi-segment memory flushes and background merges, and exposes a high-throughput HTTP search API delivering sub-15ms queries across 100,000 documents.
useCases: Enterprise Knowledge Base Documentation Search: Internal developer portals hosting hundreds of thousands of engineering design docs and markdown pages need fast keyword and phrase search. The engine indexes markdown content into inverted posting lists, ranking documentation snippets with BM25 relevance scores and serving search queries in under 12 milliseconds. | E-Commerce Product Catalog Multi-Field Search: Online retail platforms require accurate product discovery across title, description, and brand attributes with boolean query operators. title: Real-Time Clickstream Ingestion & Aggregation with ClickHouse & Kafka
problemStatement: Modern web applications generate billions of user clickstream events (page views, button clicks, impressions, conversions) daily. Storing individual unaggregated events in relational databases like PostgreSQL causes write exhaustion, sluggish queries, and ballooning storage costs. Operating a real-time event analytics platform requires streaming click events through Apache Kafka into ClickHouse using columnar compression, ReplacingMergeTree engines for deduplication, and Materialized Views for sub-second dashboard aggregations.
useCases: High-volume web analytics dashboard (self-hosted Google Analytics / PostHog alternative) | Real-time advertising impression tracking and attribution modeling | In-app user journey funnel analysis and feature engagement tracking
problemItSolves: Ingesting 50,000+ raw click events per second without dropping records or degrading query response times | Deduplicating retransmitted streaming events using ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree engines | Precomputing rollups (hourly/daily active users, conversion funnels) via Materialized Views to enable sub-50ms dashboard queries
recruiterSignal: Comprehensive understanding of columnar OLAP database design, sorting keys, and partition pruning | Benchmarks comparing PostgreSQL vs ClickHouse query speeds on 10,000,000 rows | Production Docker Compose environment with Kafka broker, ClickHouse cluster, and Grafana dashboard

title: Custom Free-List Memory Allocator (malloc/free) with Boundary-Tag Coalescing
problemStatement: High-level language runtimes and operating systems provide standard memory allocators (`malloc`, `free`), but engineers who treat memory as an infinite abstraction struggle to diagnose memory fragmentation, cache locality penalties, and heap exhaustion in performance-critical systems. Implementing a custom heap memory allocator from raw OS virtual memory pages (`sbrk` / `mmap`) demonstrates how memory headers, boundary tags, explicit free lists, and immediate neighbor coalescing govern dynamic memory allocation.
useCases: Custom arena/pool memory allocator for high-frequency trading engines | Embedded systems allocator operating under strict deterministic heap constraints | Foundation for understanding garbage collector and runtime allocator internals
problemItSolves: Eliminating external heap fragmentation by coalescing adjacent free blocks using Knuth boundary tags | Implementing explicit segregated free lists to achieve $O(1)$ block search time for common allocation sizes | Enforcing strict 8-byte/16-byte CPU memory alignment constraints to prevent hardware bus faults
recruiterSignal: Exceptional demonstration of low-level systems programming, pointer arithmetic, and heap internals | Valgrind and AddressSanitizer test runs verifying zero memory leaks or illegal pointer dereferences | Benchmark comparing allocation throughput and memory utilization against GNU libc malloc

architectureComponents.name: Core System Engine

architectureDataFlow: Allocator requests 4MB heap chunk from OS via mmap/sbrk; Divides heap into structured blocks: 8-byte Header (size + allocated bit), Payload, and 8-byte Footer; Free blocks link into an explicit doubly linked free list; my_malloc(size) finds best-fit or first-fit free block, splits block if excess size > 32 bytes, marks allocated, returns pointer; my_free(ptr) checks neighbor headers/footers, coalesces adjacent free blocks, and re-links to free list.
